Reflect \(Z=(0,0)\) across hypotenuse \(bx+ay-ab=0\).

For a point \(P=(x_0,y_0)\) and line \(Ax+By+C=0\), the reflection is
\[
x'=x_0-\frac{2A(Ax_0+By_0+C)}{A^2+B^2},\qquad 
y'=y_0-\frac{2B(Ax_0+By_0+C)}{A^2+B^2}.
\]
Here \(A=b,\ B=a,\ C=-ab\), so
\[
Z'=\left(\frac{2ab^2}{a^2+b^2},\frac{2a^2b}{a^2+b^2}\right).
\]
Also \(X'=(-a,0)\), \(Y'=(0,-b)\).

The area is
\[
\frac12\left|\det\begin{pmatrix} a & -b \\ u+a & v \end{pmatrix}\right|
=\frac12\left|av+b(u+a)\right|,
\]
where \(Z'=(u,v)\). Substituting \(u,v\):
\[
av+bu+ab
=\frac{2a^3b+2ab^3}{a^2+b^2}+ab
=2ab+ab=3ab.
\]
Thus the area is
\[
\frac12(3ab)=\frac{3ab}{2}.
\]
Since the original right triangle has area \(\frac12 ab=1\), we have \(ab=2\), so
\[
\frac{3\cdot 2}{2}=3.
\]

\[
\boxed{3}
\]
